summary: Credential-stealer native addon masquerading as a napi-rs Linux platform binary
details: The package ships a single stripped Rust ELF Node addon (tools.linux-x64-gnu.node, ~10.4 MB) declared as `main`, so `require()`/`import` of the package invokes `napi_register_module_v1` and hands full native-code control to the binary at load time. Extracted strings in the addon include Chromium password-store and cookie harvesting artifacts (`Found login for`, `SQLITE_AUTH_USER`, `on Cookie.value when inserting`), Chromium v10/v11 decryption primitives (ChaCha20 `expand 32-byte k`), host fingerprinting (`/etc/lsb-release`, `/dev/disk/by-id/`, `network_adapters`, `gethostname`, `getifaddrs`), a TLS/HTTPS client (`ureq_proto`, TLS13), and zip packaging, alongside process/dynamic-loader symbols (`execvp`, `posix_spawnp`, `dlopen`, `connect`, `getaddrinfo`). No source, no build config, no JS wrapper — the binary is the entire package. The package name and version string mimic the naming convention of legitimate napi-rs platform-arch sub-packages (`<pkg>-linux-x64-gnu`) with a padded keyword/timestamp version tail (`3.1.41-origin-chrom-468-delete-windows-32-bit-changelog-fix-408-1785838091`), and the README only claims to be an `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu binary for new-native-tools` with no documented parent package. Loading this package on Linux x64 executes a browser-credential stealer with arbitrary command-execution and outbound-network capability on the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
